subject: Re: Hosted API — region mapping, retention, and deletion evidence
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acme-thermal.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Hughes <mark.hughes@acme-thermal.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted API — clarifications on region mapping, retention and deletion

Hi Tessa / Laura,

Thanks for sending over the questionnaire. A couple of follow-ups from our security team so we can close this section of the RFP:

1) Can you provide a canonical mapping of which customer request types (api request bodies, embeddings output, logs, KV caches, metrics/telemetry) may be stored in which region(s) for the hosted API? We need to validate that PII-containing request payloads can be constrained to us regions only.

2) For retention: what are the default retention windows for request payloads, generated outputs, and audit logs? Are there configurable TTLs per-tenant?

3) Deletion: if Acme requests an immediate purge for a specific tenant (all data related to tenant-id X), what is the SLA and what systems are involved (primary, backups, object storage snapshots)? Also what evidence do you provide that deletion occurred?

4) Are backups/replication ever stored outside the region where the primary data lives?

If you can provide short, bullet answers and any evidence files we can attach to our assessment (mapping CSV, retention policy PDF, deletion playbook), that would be ideal.

Regards,
Elena Soto
Security Analyst — Acme Thermal
security@acme-thermal.com

[Attachment: Acme-RFP-Section-B.zip (references)]

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Jan 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — clarifications on region mapping, retention and deletion

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; Rishi will follow up with the technical/forensic details and evidence. Attached: hostedapi-region-mapping.csv (region-by-data-type), hostedapi-retention-standard-2025.pdf (policy snapshot).

- Region mapping: default hosted-api tenant data (request bodies, generated outputs, embeddings) is stored in the customer-selected region at account creation (US, EU, APAC). By default, if the tenant is created in a US region we do not store the request/response content outside US regions. Short-lived telemetry & anonymized aggregates used for service health may be replicated to US-based analytics endpoints only. See attachment for full matrix.

- Retention: default retention windows (hosted API):
  * Request payloads (raw request bodies): 30 days by default; configurable down to 0 days on request (data minimization) or extended up to 365 days for customer opt-in.
  * Generated outputs (model responses / completions / embeddings): 90 days default; can be shortened to 0 days on managed contract for privacy-first customers.
  * Audit logs (authentication events, admin actions): 365 days default.
  * KV cache (inference session caches): ephemeral for hosted customers — typically 0 days persistence; caches persist only for the life of the inference session and are not written to long-term storage unless customer enables session logging.

- Deletion & SLA: On a verified tenant erasure request we perform a staged purge: primary objects and database records are removed within 72 hours; object storage deletions propagate immediately but may remain in immutable snapshots for a short window until snapshots are rotated. Backups are rotated and purged according to the backup retention schedule; permanent removal from all retention systems typically completes within 30 days. We provide evidence via a deletion attestation (PDF) and a detailed job log.

- Backups/replication: backups for US-region tenants are stored in US-only regions by default. Cross-region replication only occurs if explicitly enabled for redundancy and is documented in the tenant config.

Next steps: Rishi can provide the deletion playbook and an example attestation we provide to customers. Neha looped in for any contractual language or EEA-specific clauses.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: hostedapi-region-mapping.csv (CSV)]
[Attachment: hostedapi-retention-standard-2025.pdf (PDF)]

Elena — quick commercial note so you have it for procurement: we can contractually lock a tenant to a single region and add a Data Residency addendum that explicitly disallows cross-region backups unless Acme requests it. If you want the shortest retention windows (0 days) we treat that as an enterprise privacy option and will include the attestation process in the SOW.

Tessa and Rishi — happy to discuss price delta if they want region-lock + 0-day retention for logs/requests.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Thanks — that helps. A couple of follow-ups before we close the control:

1) For deletions: can you confirm the maximum time between a verified purge request and removal from ALL backup snapshots in the worst case? We need an explicit upper bound we can put in our control matrix.

2) Audit logs: are there separate retention and export controls for admin/audit logs vs request logs? We want to ensure privileged admin actions can be retained for our internal compliance 7 years if needed (we know defaults differ).

3) KV cache: you mentioned ephemeral — does Redwood ever serialize KV caches to durable storage for debugging or support purposes? If so, what is the process and can it be disabled?

4) Evidence: if you could attach the deletion-playbook-steps.txt and an example customer deletion attestation that would be ideal.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Regards,
Elena Soto
Security Analyst — Acme Thermal

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@acme-thermal.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 15:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Hosted API — clarifications on region mapping, retention and deletion

Hi Elena — Rishi from Security here, following up with the technical details and the requested artifacts (attached).

Answers to your numbered points:

1) Worst-case full purge from backups: our operational SLA for a verified, authenticated tenant-wide erase is 30 days maximum for complete removal from all backup and snapshot layers. We document the job run, objects removed, and snapshot rotation IDs in the attestation. In practice the primary deletion completes within 72 hours and backup rotation usually finalizes inside 14–21 days unless there is a legal hold.

2) Audit logs: there are separate categories — (a) request logs (API calls, payload metadata), (b) system audit logs (admin actions, configuration changes), and (c) security logs (intrusion detection, auth events). Each category has independent retention controls. For hosted customers we offer extension options for system audit logs up to 7 years (additional subscription). Exports can be generated as encrypted bundles and pushed to a customer S3/GCS bucket or provided as signed attestations.

3) KV cache serialization: by default KV caches are not persisted to durable storage. On rare occasions we capture session traces for debugging; this happens only with explicit customer consent or through a signed support authorization that includes the session id and time window. Customers can completely disable session trace capture in the tenant configuration (we include a boolean flag: session_trace_enabled=false).

4) Evidence: attached are the deletion-playbook-steps.txt (internal playbook excerpt we provide a redacted copy of for customers) and a sample deletion attestation PDF (redacted example). We also provide a CSV manifest mapping object IDs removed and snapshot rotation markers when a purge job runs.

Attachments in this email: deletion-playbook-steps.txt (TXT), hosteda-purge-attestation-example.pdf (PDF), purge-manifest-20260120.csv (CSV).

If you want, we can run a short (non-destructive) audit job showing the tenant's current residency/retention configuration and provide a signed attestation for your records. Let me know and I will schedule the run and provide the DocuSign-ready attestation.

Best regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
